what_this_is: Every dataset this repository REDISTRIBUTES that it did not author. Redistribution is the trigger, not use: reading a source at build time is not covered here, shipping its rows is. The repository's own code is Apache-2.0 (see LICENSE); that licence does not and cannot extend to the rows below.
why_it_exists: biology_as_code/NOTICE had no third-party section while MASTER_CROSSWALK.tsv shipped 2,797 rows derived from a source this project's own notes assess as non-commercial. The gap was not that the licence was unknown — working_map_nutrition/VMH_REFERENCE.md had the analysis since July. It was that the analysis never reached the published repository.
not_legal_advice: Engineering hygiene, assembled from the sources' own statements and this project's prior assessment. Confirm with the rights holder and with counsel before any commercial use or relicensing.

entries.declared_licence: Academic and research use with citation; commercial use restricted (VMH FAQ 26)
entries.licence_note: VMH DOES state terms, found 2026-08-29 at the licence_url above, verbatim: "VMH content is freely available for academic and research use; please cite the appropriate resources. Several data sources integrated into VMH carry their own licences, some of which restrict commercial use – please check the terms of the original source for such data. For commercial-licensing questions, please contact ines.thiele [at] universityofgalway [dot] ie". Two corrections to what this entry said before. (1) The previous 'CC BY-NC 2.0' came from this project's own working_map_nutrition/VMH_REFERENCE.md and is supported by no VMH source; do not restate it. (2) The claim that vmh.life returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval was FALSE and was load-bearing — it is why these terms went unread for a month. One fetching tool was blocked; plain curl gets 200 on the site, the FAQ and every /_api/ endpoint. A tool being blocked is not a source being silent. Still OPEN, and narrowly so: the granted use is academic and research with citation, and the FAQ does not address redistributing a DERIVED COMPILATION in a public Apache-2.0 repository, which is exactly what MASTER_CROSSWALK.tsv is. Confirm before any commercial use.

what_is_redistributed.note: 8 of 12 columns. The individual cells are largely facts — chemical formulae and registry identifiers are not creative expression. The exposure is the COMPILATION: 2,797 curated rows extracted wholesale, and in particular the cross-reference mapping between VMH, HMDB, KEGG, ChEBI and PubChem, which is the curatorial work that gives the table its value. VMH is maintained in the EU, where the sui generis database right restricts substantial extraction independently of copyright.

entries.conflict: This repository is Apache-2.0, which permits commercial use. A CC BY-NC source cannot be redistributed under those terms. Until resolved, the crosswalk should be treated as non-commercial regardless of the repository licence, and MASTER_CROSSWALK.NOTICE.md says so next to the file.
remedies_available: Confirm the operative licence with VMH directly. The declared value above is OPEN.
Swap the backend to Human-GEM (CC BY 4.0) and regenerate — the path this project's own VMH_REFERENCE.md already identified for a commercial build.

Reduce to identifiers only: drop `name` (VMH's fullName labels) and rebuild the cross-references from each registry directly rather than from VMH's mapping. This removes the compilation exposure but discards the curatorial join that is the table's value.
Obtain a licence from the rights holder.
entries.columns_derived: 9 of 12, not 8: vmh, name, formula, hmdb, kegg, chebi, pubchem, seed (VMH's own SEED2VMH_translation.csv), and inchiKey. NOTE inchiKey is OPEN in all 2,797 rows — the upstream VMH export shipped none, so it is an empty column inherited, not a processing defect. Any plan treating InChIKey as an available join key is building on nothing.
entries.alternative_sources_checked: BiGG Models (bigg.ucsd.edu/models/Recon3D) also distributes Recon3D and is NOT an escape hatch: BiGG is freely available for non-commercial use, and its model page carries 'Copyright (c) 2019 The Regents of the University of California'. Checked 2026-08-29. Note the trap: secondary sources describe BiGG content as CC-BY-like 'unrestricted reuse if cited' — that is the open-access licence of the BiGG PAPERS, not of the models. bigg.ucsd.edu/license was not fetched directly, so this remains OPEN pending that read. Evidence saved privately in nutri-collective/docs/licence-evidence/.

entries.attribution: Open Food Facts contributors. https://world.openfoodfacts.org — data under the Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0.
entries.licence_note: Open Food Facts publishes its database under ODbL 1.0. ODbL is SHARE-ALIKE: publicly using a derived database obliges you to offer that derived database under ODbL, and attribution is required in all cases. This is a real obligation, not a courtesy, and it is not satisfied by the repository's Apache-2.0 licence.

what_is_redistributed.note: 67 meal fixtures declare `OpenFoodFacts (fallback macros)` in their own nutrition_provenance block, alongside USDA FDC. OFF supplied macro values where USDA had none. Whether 67 fixtures constitute a 'derived database' under ODbL or merely a produced work using insubstantial extracts is a genuine open question; attribution is required either way and is the cheap half.

entries.conflict: Attribution was absent from NOTICE until 2026-08-29 while the repo was public. Share-alike status is unresolved.
